title: Bandwidth Control API, SDK and Terraform shape

prose.text: Bandwidth Control is fully API-manageable; the console is not the only plane. This subject holds names and enums; behavior is in the sibling subjects.

prose.label: Rule fields.
prose.text: {{min-max-fields}} Those are the console's guaranteed and maximum percentages ([[zia.bandwidth-control.allocation]]). {{rule-scope-fields}} {{device-fields-not-in-help}} {{protocols-spec}} {{protocols-terraform}} The two protocol lists disagree {{divergence:protocol-vocabulary}}. {{tf-location-caps}} The Help location limit differs {{divergence:locations-per-rule}}. Rule order, state and rank semantics: [[zia.bandwidth-control.rules]]; provider reorder behavior: [[zia.terraform.rule-order.registry]].

prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{tf-class-resources}} {{tf-wrappers-update-existing}} The Terraform bandwidth control rule resource is documented as OneAPI-only {{tf-rule-oneapi-only}}, and whether the class resources share the restriction is not stated {{gap:tf-classes-oneapi-only}}. Terraform destroy semantics in general: [[zia.terraform.delete-detach]]. The Large Files size field is named differently in the schema and the SDK {{divergence:file-size-field-name}}.

checks.do: Whether the live response for a class matches the type and size names before relying on them.
Whether the protocol values in use are accepted by the service, given that the schema and the provider lists differ.

min-max-fields.statement: The rule's minimum and maximum are the integer fields minBandwidth and maxBandwidth, documented as percentages of a location's bandwidth per selected class, covering uploads and downloads together.

expect.description: The minimum percentage of a location’s bandwidth you want to be guaranteed for each selected bandwidth class. This percentage includes bandwidth for uploads and downloads.
The maximum percentage of a location’s bandwidth to be guaranteed for each selected bandwidth class. This percentage includes bandwidth for uploads and downloads.

rule-scope-fields.statement: Besides locations, location groups, time windows, labels, bandwidth classes and protocols, the rule schema also carries devices, deviceGroups and deviceTrustLevels.

expect.description: A Boolean value that indicates whether the rule is a default rule

quotes: The logical relationship between the categories is AND, and the rule conditions within each category have their own set of logical operators applied, explained as follows:
Where [ Locations OR Location Groups ] AND

expect.description: Labels that are applicable to the rule. This field is not applicable to the Lite API.

device-fields-not-in-help.statement: The console Help groups the rule conditions as Where (locations or location groups), When (time) and What (bandwidth classes and protocols), so the schema's device, device group and device trust level fields have no counterpart among the conditions it documents.
device-fields-not-in-help.conditions: Rests on the three condition categories the Help page lists and on a search of that page, which has no occurrence of device.

protocols-spec.statement: The API schema lists these rule protocol values: ANY_RULE, DOHTTPS_RULE, TUNNELSSL_RULE, HTTP_PROXY, FOHTTP_RULE, FTP_RULE, HTTPS_RULE, HTTP_RULE, SSL_RULE and TUNNEL_RULE.

protocols-terraform.statement: The Terraform bandwidth rule resource requires at least one protocol and validates it with the URL Filtering protocol list, `supportedURLFilteringProtocols`: SMRULEF_ZPA_BROKERS_RULE, ANY_RULE, TCP_RULE, UDP_RULE, DOHTTPS_RULE, TUNNELSSL_RULE, HTTP_PROXY, FOHTTP_RULE, FTP_RULE, HTTPS_RULE, HTTP_RULE, SSL_RULE, TUNNEL_RULE, WEBSOCKETSSL_RULE and WEBSOCKET_RULE.

tf-location-caps.statement: The Terraform bandwidth rule schema allows at most 8 locations and 32 location groups per rule.

quotes: setIDsSchemaTypeCustom(intPtr(8), "Name-ID pairs of locations for which rule must be applied")
setIDsSchemaTypeCustom(intPtr(32), "Name-ID pairs of the location groups to which the rule must be applied.")

class-type-enum.statement: A bandwidth class has a read-only type with the values ANY, NONE, BANDWIDTH_CAT_WEBCONF, BANDWIDTH_CAT_VOIP, BANDWIDTH_CAT_GENERAL_SURFING, BANDWIDTH_CAT_LARGE_FILE, BANDWIDTH_CAT_SALES, BANDWIDTH_CAT_FINANCE, BANDWIDTH_CAT_MEDIA and BANDWIDTH_CAT_FSHARE.

types-match-predefined.statement: The eight non-generic type values appear to correspond to the eight predefined classes: five Cloud Applications classes (General Surfing, Sales/Support Apps, Finance, Streaming Media, File Share), Large Files, Web Conferencing and VoIP.
types-match-predefined.conditions: Derived by matching the type names to the Help class names and the count of eight; no source states the mapping. How a custom class is typed on the wire is not shown.

file-size-enum.statement: The Large Files size values are ANY, NONE, FILE_5MB, FILE_10MB, FILE_50MB, FILE_100MB, FILE_250MB, FILE_500MB and FILE_1GB in the API; the Terraform resource accepts FILE_5MB, FILE_10MB, FILE_50MB, FILE_100MB, FILE_250MB, FILE_500MB and FILE_1GB (not ANY or NONE).

application-values.statement: The class applications field takes ANY, NONE, NETSUITE, DROPBOX, BOXNET, YOUTUBE, METACAFE, HULU, DAILYMOTION, SHOUTCAST, SALESFORCE_1, SKYPE, WEBEX, GOTOMEETING, LIVEMEETING, CONNECT and INTERCALL. Terraform accepts only WEBEX, GOTOMEETING, LIVEMEETING, INTERCALL and CONNECT for a web conferencing class, and only SKYPE (or an empty value) for a VoIP class.

quotes: return fmt.Errorf("application %q is not valid for type %q", app, classType)

tf-class-resources.statement: Terraform splits the class object into three resources: zia_bandwidth_classes (urls, url_categories, web_applications; no type or applications field), zia_bandwidth_classes_file_size (defaults type to BANDWIDTH_CAT_LARGE_FILE) and zia_bandwidth_classes_web_conferencing (type BANDWIDTH_CAT_WEBCONF or BANDWIDTH_CAT_VOIP, plus applications).

quotes: "web_applications": { Type: schema.TypeSet, Optional: true, Elem: &schema.Schema{Type: schema.TypeString}, }, }, } }

tf-rule-oneapi-only.statement: The Terraform bandwidth control rule documentation says the resource is only supported through Zscaler OneAPI.

quotes: Bandwidth control rule resource is only supported via Zscaler OneAPI.

protocol-vocabulary.summary: Which protocol values a Bandwidth Control rule accepts

positions.says: The API schema lists ten values and none of WEBSOCKET_RULE, WEBSOCKETSSL_RULE, TCP_RULE, UDP_RULE or SMRULEF_ZPA_BROKERS_RULE.
The provider validates against the URL Filtering list, which includes the WebSocket values.

protocol-vocabulary.impact: A configuration using a value only the provider accepts may be rejected by the service, and a value the provider rejects cannot be sent through Terraform even if the service accepts it.

locations-per-rule.summary: How many locations one rule can reference

quotes: setIDsSchemaTypeCustom(intPtr(8), "Name-ID pairs of locations for which rule must be applied")

positions.says: The Terraform schema caps locations at 8 per bandwidth rule.
Ranges and Limitations lists 32 locations per rule for all policy rule types.

locations-per-rule.impact: A rule that needs 9 to 32 locations cannot be written through the provider; use location groups (32) or split the rule, even if the service would accept more.

positions.says: The API schema names the field getfileSize.

quotes: self.file_size = config["fileSize"] if "fileSize" in config else None

file-size-field-name.impact: One of the two spellings may never be populated; code that reads or writes the Large Files size should confirm the wire name against a live response.

custom-class-type.title: The type value of a custom class
custom-class-type.detail: The API type enumeration lists only the eight predefined categories plus ANY and NONE. What type a custom class returns, and whether the general zia_bandwidth_classes resource ever sets one, is not shown.

file-size-wire-name.title: Live name of the Large Files size field
file-size-wire-name.detail: See the file-size-field-name divergence: the schema says getfileSize, the SDK reads fileSize.

tf-classes-oneapi-only.title: Whether the Terraform bandwidth class resources also require OneAPI
tf-classes-oneapi-only.blocks: saying that bandwidth classes cannot be managed with legacy credentials
tf-classes-oneapi-only.detail: Unverified legacy statement: the legacy catalog said the three bandwidth class resources require Zscaler OneAPI; only the bandwidth control rule page says so in the provider docs. Apply a class with legacy credentials in a scratch tenant.
